cells.tense: You're at the end of the work and the work knows it — here, with your hands on it, not looking past it yet.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to one person, what this finished thing gave you — then let it go without tidying it up first.
cells.core:
You know the difference between a thing that's done and a thing you're avoiding finishing. What you've been looking after has actually arrived, and you're standing in it rather than bracing for the next demand. Nothing is tearing at you to fix it further, and the proof is that it grew while you held it. A full crate at the end of the row, set down, noted — and the next row is going in, but not yet. That's the shape of it when it's going right, and it's not a small achievement.

When something here is finished, say what it gave you, out loud, once — and then let it leave. That's the whole act. Through the gate, the ground you've been standing on gets to feed something new, and the quiet that follows a thing actually being complete is yours to keep.

cells.tense: You're already at the next thing in your head — living in a finished version of this that nobody else has been told about yet.
cells.ask: Write down what this thing looks like when it's done — then put the paper away and come back to what's actually in front of you.
cells.core:
You're picturing the next stage before this one is actually standing — what the trip looks like once it's over, who'll be there, how it'll feel. The picturing is coming from something unprocessed underneath, and it's pulling your effort out of the place it needs to be right now. The planning is real work. It's just not the work in front of you yet. Fed by what's actually happened, the same imagining lands as a picture of the harvest already on the table — a report, not a rehearsal.

Write down what done looks like, once, and put the paper somewhere you won't see it today. That's the ask — and what it gets you is your hands back on the part that has to happen before any of it is true.

cells.tense: You're still at the door you walked through — the finishing moved on without you, and part of you is standing where the room used to be.
cells.ask: Pick up the thread at the smallest possible point — one email, one dish, one paragraph — and do only that.
cells.core:
What you were looking after has moved past the point where it needed your hands, and you're standing at the threshold holding a shape that's already gone. The care isn't missing — it's pointed at something that isn't there to receive it anymore. The hoping runs on the same fuel as the working, just aimed backward. When it's going right, the row you planted comes up and you're already thinking about what goes in next, because the growing itself was the point and not whatever came after.

Put your hand back on the smallest piece of what you're actually building — one email, one dish, one paragraph — and let that be the whole action. Not a leap, not a decision. Just the next thing, which gives you something to be working on instead of something to be waiting for.

cells.tense: You're looking after a lot of small things right now without ever putting your hand up about the fact that you're the one doing it.
cells.ask: Say 'this was mine' about one piece of the work, out loud, to someone standing near enough to hear it.
cells.core:
You're the one keeping the parts of this alive — the checking, the feeding, the putting things back — and you talk about it like it runs itself. It doesn't. The garden grew because someone was out there with a watering can, which is not a small thing, and the fact that it's invisible is the cost of how well it's being done. Named plainly, that same looking-after changes shape in the room — the hand that did it gets to rest without anything collapsing.

Say 'this was mine' once, out loud, to someone near enough to hear it. That's the act. It makes the work visible — and the ground it gives back is one you can stand on like you made it, because you did.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim would be saying what the person's cultivation or endings actually are in their life — the record only gives the capacity, the seat and the condition. A reader could reasonably say the tension described isn't what's happening for them, so every cell is written narrow enough to be refused and still leave something to use. The asks are simple physical acts that teach something even if the read is wrong. The line most at risk of serving the writer is the closing sentence of each core, so no core is allowed a verdict about who the person is, only about how this capacity behaves in this part of a life.
